Sean — quick legal read attached. High-level notes: 1) We should not remove the general liability cap — that exposes company to unlimited risk if combined with warranty/indemnity carveouts. 2) A targeted data-breach carveout is acceptable but we recommend tying any carveout to a fixed aggregate cap (suggested: $3M USD equivalent) and a sublimit for regulatory fines. 3) Indemnity redlines: HelioRx's version expands indemnity for third-party claims substantially; propose reverting to our standard indemnity language but add breach-specific indemnity limited to the breach cap. 4) Warranty: their requested warranty duration and remedies are more expansive than standard — propose a 90-day warranty period and remedies limited to repair/replace and service credits.

If sales is requesting flexibility on cap/indemnity, this requires exec approval because it changes enterprise risk exposure and will need an accounting disclosure for reserved liabilities. For clarity, if we accept a $3M breach carveout + parity on indemnity with the sublimit, legal would sign off with exec authorization.

Attached: HelioRx_Redlines_v3_LegalNotes.docx (summary inline in the doc).

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Redwood pilot — commercial and legal questions

Team — pricing impact analysis attached (summary below).

Summary: 35% off list for year one on a base usage estimate ~ $1.2M ARR run-rate = ~$420k gross revenue reduction year one. If we structure the concession as: 1) 20% year-one discount + 15% backloaded credit tied to 12-months usage thresholds, AND 2) require minimum committed spend (12-month minimum, with true-up quarterly), we recover ~70% of the margin loss. Additional levers: migrate customer to Dedicated at month 3 (adds predictable unit economics) or require incremental onboarding fee to cover custom PII handling.

Recommended commercial package for exec consideration: - Approve data-breach carveout cap at $3M (USD equivalent) tied to defined breach categories and mandatory incident-response requirements. - Approve a split discount: 20% upfront year-one + 10–15% credit subject to usage milestones and prepayment. - Require commitment term to be 24 months; include early-termination fee if they downsize below committed usage.

This package gets us within 10% of target margin and aligns incentives. If execs want a deeper concession (35% straight off), finance will need to sign a one-time margin waiver and update forecasts.

Marissa Cole
Director, Deals & Strategic Pricing
Redwood Inference
Attachment: HelioRx_Pricing_Impact_Analysis.xlsx (xlsx)
